claims_extracted.claim: Each of the thirteen T1-era NSSs was described as nine IBM RT systems processors running Berkeley UNIX, linked by two Token Rings and connected via Ethernet to attached networks.
claims_extracted.notes: Confirmed as a claim made by this retrospective report; seek contemporary BOMs beneath it.

claims_extracted.claim: Figure 14 depicts four IBM RT Packet Switching Processors, an IBM RT Routing Control Processor, an IBM RT External Packet Switching Processor, two IBM PS/2 Model 80 management systems, dual Token Rings, WACS/DSU-CSU on the T1 side, and Ethernet on the client side; three backup IBM RTs are omitted from the drawing.
claims_extracted.notes: Confirmed as a claim made by this retrospective report.

claims_extracted.claim: NSS hardware/software was assembled and configured at an Ann Arbor depot before site installation, with regional personnel participating.
claims_extracted.notes: Confirmed as a claim made by this retrospective report.

claims_extracted.claim: A SESQUINET shipment anecdote describes seven RTs and three racks, creating an unresolved scoped discrepancy with the generic nine-RT NSS description.
claims_extracted.notes: Confirmed as a claim made by this retrospective report; preserve both claims and resolve with shipment/site inventory records.

claims_extracted.claim: The Ann Arbor NOC operated around the clock, grew from four to eighteen staff, displayed NSS/link status, and used two IBM 4831 systems for network-management/statistics/information functions.
claims_extracted.notes: Confirmed as a claim made by this retrospective report; recover contemporary NOC hardware/software inventory and Site Manual.

conflicts: NSS processor count (open): generic architecture states nine IBM RTs; SESQUINET shipping recollection states seven RTs and three racks for that delivery.
